consensus_summary: Fire primarily symbolizes God's holy/consuming presence, expressed as judgment/destruction of evil and purification/refinement of the faithful (with common secondary senses for Holy Spirit, hell, trials, and minority senses for word/zeal).
book_summary: Fire is God's all-consuming presence that reveals, refines, or destroys according to what encounters it; the same fire sustains the bush, refines silver, preserves the covered, and consumes uncovered wickedness.
consensus_core_identification: God's holy/consuming presence that both judges/consumes evil and purifies what is preserved.
book_core_identification: God's all-consuming presence that reveals/refines/destroys (or sustains/preserves) according to the object encountered.
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: both identify fire as the single divine presence/holiness whose effect (consume vs. purify/preserve) is determined by what it meets. Book wording ('reveals... according to what encounters it'; bush/Daniel preservation) adds no new referent and excludes none of the consensus primary cases; polyvalent alternatives remain compatible sub-applications rather than rival cores.
strongest_objection: Some consensus responses weight pure judgment/eschatological fire as the default primary while treating presence as an alternative, so the book's unified-presence framing could be read as a mild re-prioritization.
